decode_modes.bypass: loop only during prefill (default for loglikelihood evals)
decode_modes.full: loop every decode step (default for generation results)
decode_modes.first_n: loop the first n generated tokens

claims.bypass: no wall-clock cost; -1.5% is run-to-run noise from a leaner KV-write path
claims.full: ~22% slowdown for K=3 on a 4/36 layer window
claims.cost_model: 1 + (K-1) * (b-a+1)/N extra layer passes in the loop region

tables1619.table17_claim: 11 of 12 tabulated cells non-negative under the better of {K=2 Euler, K=1 Heun}

search_protocol.space: window center in [0.40N, 0.70N] x {n=3,4,6} x {2,3} x {NAIVE, EMA, EULER} x {FIRST, LAST}
search_protocol.variance: <=0.02 pp on >=10k-example benchmarks; <=0.5 pp on <=1k-example ones

table20_cache.invariant: net cache delta of the whole procedure is exactly b-a+1 entries regardless of K
table20_cache.mechanism: DynamicCache.update() always appends; snapshot/crop is the cheapest restore (App C.2)

selection_rule_ambiguity.paper: Fig 6 claims 7 of 9 optimal window centers fall in 0.45-0.60, naming only Llama-3.2-1B (earlier) and Qwen1.5-MoE (later) as outliers
selection_rule_ambiguity.explanation: Fig 6 plots one best window per checkpoint while Table 6 lists several winning windows per checkpoint. Under the largest-delta rule Moonlight-16B-A3B is placed by its OBQA cell [8-11] (0.352, outside), so Moonlight becomes a third outlier and the count is 6 of 9; taking Moonlight's [11-14] cell (0.463) instead restores the paper's 7 of 9. The paper does not state which winning cell each Fig 6 marker uses.

depth_fraction.window_width_rule: the reported winning windows are n=3 or n=4 except Qwen1.5-MoE [10,13]

sub_1b_shift_earlier.tension: Sec 3.2 calls sub-1B earlier while Fig 6 places Qwen3-0.6B inside the band; only Llama-3.2-1B is the named sub-1B outlier

table21_patch_surface.notes: layer-mode default; routing pinned per layer

implementation_notes: monkey patch on the top-level decoder class; reversible
DynamicCache shim re-adds seen_tokens/get_max_length/get_usable_length for MLA remote code
KV cache writes are the only side effect; no auxiliary state beyond a Theta(W) buffer
